relationships.subject: anandamide
relationships.evidence_quote: decreased by 98% ± 0.5% following the application of 10 μM AEA

relationships.subject: CB1
relationships.evidence_quote: CB1 is responsible for the majority of inhibition of VGSC currents by AEA and that this is mediated via a GTP-dependent mechanism

relationships.subject: WIN 55,212-2
relationships.evidence_quote: The synthetic CB1 agonist WIN 55,212-2 (10 μM) strongly reduced VGSC current amplitude in wild-type neurons but was substantially less effective in Cnr1−/− neurons

relationships.subject: AM4113
relationships.evidence_quote: The maximum fractional block of VGSC currents by AEA was reduced from 0.96 (n=7) to 0.27 (n=6) by the neutral CB1 antagonist AM4113

relationships.subject: 2-arachidonoylglycerol
relationships.evidence_quote: 2-AG, another endocannabinoid that activates CB1, did not inhibit VGSC currents even at high concentration

key_findings: Anandamide, but not 2-AG, inhibits somatic VGSC currents in neocortical neurons via intracellular CB1 and a GTP-dependent G-protein pathway.
CB1-VGSC coupling is absent at boutons, axons and dendrites.
